title: Prompt Injection
description: Adversarial inputs can cause unintended behaviors by manipulating the model's prompts through direct or indirect injection techniques.
common_patterns: Indirect injection via tool outputs or context
mitigation: Input validation, output filtering, privilege separation between system and user prompts, and prompt encapsulation.

title: Insecure Output Handling
description: Model outputs are not validated or sanitized before downstream processing, allowing potential XSS, SSRF, or other injection attacks.
common_patterns: Dynamic code execution from model output
mitigation: Treat all model output as untrusted. Apply output validation, encoding, and sandboxing before passing to downstream components.

title: Training Data Poisoning
description: Malicious data injected into training corpora can introduce backdoors, biases, or vulnerabilities that manifest at inference time.
mitigation: Verify data supply chains, use provenance tracking, apply content filtering on training data, and monitor for distribution shifts.

title: Model Denial of Service
description: Resource exhaustion through abnormally large inputs, recursive calls, or strategic input that triggers expensive processing.
mitigation: Implement input size limits, rate limiting, quota systems, and resource monitoring. Detect and reject anomalously expensive requests.

title: Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
description: Vulnerabilities in the ML supply chain including third-party models, packages, and pre-trained components.
mitigation: Use signed model artifacts, pin dependency versions, verify checksums, and audit third-party components before deployment.

title: Excessive Agency
description: LLM-powered systems taking actions that are unintended, irreversible, or beyond the system's security boundaries.
mitigation: Limit tool permissions, require human approval for sensitive actions, implement rate limiting on tool calls, and apply least-privilege to model agency.

title: System Prompt Leakage
description: Exposing system-level instructions, configuration, or internal context through prompts, errors, or outputs.
mitigation: Restrict system prompt access, mask internal context in outputs, implement prompt obfuscation, and sanitize error messages.

title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
description: Manipulation of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems through poisoned vector stores or embedding spaces.
mitigation: Input sanitization for vector stores, tenant isolation, content trust scoring, and retrieval result validation.

title: Misinformation
description: LLM produces plausible but false, harmful, or misleading outputs presented as factual.
mitigation: Implement fact-checking pipelines, citation requirements, uncertainty quantification, and ground outputs against trusted sources.

title: Model Theft
description: Unauthorized access, extraction, or replication of proprietary model weights and capabilities.
mitigation: Rate limiting, access logging, output perturbation, model watermarking, and monitoring for anomalous query patterns.
